2010 Consensus First Team All-American }} '''Wesley JaMarr Johnson''' (born July 11, 1987 in [[Corsicana, Texas]]) is an [[United States|American]] basketball player who plays college basketball for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. He is one of the top players in college basketball and is projected as a high lottery pick for the 2010 NBA draft.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=4765334 |title=Dana O'Neil: Big East early season review - ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=December 23, 2009 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}}{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=4818431 |title=Jay Bilas' Midseason All-American team - ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=January 12, 2010 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}} ==High School== In high school he averaged 15.2 points, 9.7 rebounds and 4.3 blocks as a senior at [[Corsicana High School]]. He was a first-team all-district pick in 2004 and 2005. He also played for the Dallas Mustangs [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team. ==College== === 2006-07 === As a freshman at [[Iowa State University|Iowa State]], Johnson was named to the Big 12 all-Rookie team and earned honorable mention freshman All-America honors after averaging 12.3 points and 7.9 rebounds, starting 30 of 31 games. Johnson's highlights from his freshman year included 14 points and 13 rebounds in win against Missouri, including the game-winner on a tip-in with 1.6 seconds left. He also scored 17 points at No. 10 [[Texas A&M Aggies|Texas A&M]]. === 2007-08 === Johnson missed five games and played with an injured ankle throughout the majority of the season. He still was named an honorable mention all-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] selection after averaging 12.4 points and 4.0 rebounds per game. Johnson scored 20 points behind a 5-of-11 effort from 3-point range against eventual NCAA Champion [[Kansas Jayhawks|Kansas]].{{cite web|url=http://www.cyclones.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=46664&SPID=4252&DB_OEM_ID=10700&ATCLID=329810&Q_SEASON=2007 |title=Wesley Johnson - Iowa State University Athletics Official Web Site - www.CYCLONES.com - The home of Iowa State Cyclone Sports |publisher=www.CYCLONES.com |date= |accessdate=March 22, 2010}} === 2008-09 === Johnson made the decision to transfer following the 2008 season, and selected [[Syracuse Orange|Syracuse]]. Per NCAA transfer rules, he had to sit out the 2008-09 season, leaving him with two years of college eligibility.{{cite web|url=http://media.www.dailyorange.com/media/storage/paper522/news/2008/05/08/Sports/Mbb-Syracuse.Lands.Iowa.State.Tranfer.Johnson-3385520.shtml |title=Daily Orange - MBB | Syracuse lands Iowa State tranfer Johnson |publisher=Media.www.dailyorange.com |date= |accessdate=March 22, 2010}} === 2009-10 === Johnson became a starter for the Orange in his first year with the team. In November 2009 he was named MVP of the 2K Coaches Classic after scoring 25 points in a Syracuse victory over [[North Carolina Tar Heels|North Carolina]].{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/gameflash/2009/11/20/61816_recap.html?eref=sircrc |title=North Carolina vs. Syracuse - Recap - November 20, 2009 - College Basketball - SI.com |publisher=Sportsillustrated.cnn.com |date= |accessdate=March 22, 2010}} Johnson would score 17 points and grab 10 rebounds as Syracuse knocked off then-No. 10 Florida on December 10, 2009.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=293440057 |title=Syracuse Orange vs. Florida Gators - Box Score - December 10, 2009 - ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=December 10, 2009 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}} In his first game of Big East play, Johnson scored 20 points and grabbed a career high 19 rebounds as Syracuse defeated Seton Hall 80-73 on December 29, 2009.{{cite web|author=9:00 PM ET, December 29, 2009Prudential Center, Newark, NJ |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=293642550 |title=Syracuse Orange vs. Seton Hall Pirates - Box Score - December 29, 2009 - ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=December 29, 2009 |accessdate=March 22, 2010}} Johnson was named Big East Player of the Year on March 9, 2010, finishing with season averages of 16.0 points and 8.4 rebounds.{{cite web|author=Dennis Nett / The Post-Standard |url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2010/03/syracuses_wes_johnson_wins_big.html |title=Syracuse's Wes Johnson wins Big East Player of the Year. On March 29, 2010 Wes Johnson was selected to AP All American. | syracuse.com |publisher=Blog.syracuse.com |date= |accessdate=March 22, 2010}} On March 29, 2010, Johnson was named a First Team AP All American.http://www.9wsyr.com/news/local/story/Wes-Johnson-makes-AP-All-American-team/3bmiBqS9R0ymLLOSYmIgvQ.cspx On April 12, 2010, Johnson declared himself eligible for the NBA draft, forgoing his final year of college eligibility. http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2010/04/wes_johnson_leaves_his_home_in.html He has signed with [[sports agent]] [[Rob Pelinka]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/article/139218|title=Pelinka Signs Two Potential NBA Lottery Picks; Falk Inks Monroe|accessdate=2010-05-13|date=2010-05-11|publisher=[[Street & Smith]]|work=[[SportsBusiness Daily]]|author=Mullen, Liz}} ==See also== * [[2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans]] == References == {{Reflist}} ==External links== * [http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=2690&sport=176&roster=228&path=mbasket SUAthletics.com] {{Syracuse Orange basketball}} {{Syracuse_basketball}} {{2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans}} {{Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Johnson, Wesley}} [[Category:Syracuse Orange men's basketball players]] [[Category:Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Texas]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:1987 births]] [[Category:American basketball players]] [[fr:Wesley Johnson]] [[lv:Veslijs Džonsons]]
